description: Trigger evaluation set for the identify skill: requests that SHOULD activate coverage-driven Profile interviewing, and near-miss negatives that should route elsewhere. Used by the develop trigger smoke test and by `develop optimize`.
should_trigger: help me populate my Working Style
my Personality facet is still all template, can we fix that
you don't really know much about me yet, let's change that
walk me through some questions so my profile isn't so empty
should_not_trigger: what does the McAdams life-story method actually measure
update my Focus: heads-down on the launch this week
change my salutation to Mr. Golden
draft my bio for the company website
write up my working style as a one-pager for my team
what is the capital of Australia
summarize the article I just pasted
set a reminder for my dentist appointment tomorrow
notes: Positives are the named triggers plus the proactive case: a facet found thin or template-empty pulls identify in even when the user never says identify. Near-misses are deliberately adjacent. A world-fact question about a framework (Big Five, McAdams) is research, not identify: identify asks the user about themselves, never about the world. A user-dictated update ('update my Focus', 'change my salutation') is a direct edit under the normal write path (Profile/Profile.md, Rules), no interview needed: identify is for eliciting, not transcribing. A prose file written under instruction ('draft my bio', 'write up my working style') is editorial's; identify writes only the approved proposal batch into Profile. Generic clerical, arithmetic, and translation tasks are out of scope.
